text:
Rafael Mendes: quick final pass on the hosted overload mitigation runbook section: “changing breaker configs during an incident”

Rafael Mendes: we need to be explicit about:
1) what knobs exist (per (model,region,tier) breaker open/close thresholds + cooldown)
2) what’s allowed as an emergency mitigation vs what’s not
3) who can do it (and how we audit)

Rafael Mendes: can folks weigh in today so we can stop bikeshedding and ship the runbook update?

Christine Wong: +1. i can add the exact breaker params we support today, but we should lock down permissions.

Christine Wong: right now the routing service has:
- `open_threshold` (signal-based)
- `close_threshold`
- `cooldown_seconds`
- `half_open_max_rps`
- `min_samples`

Christine Wong: plus the feature flag path (enable/disable overload protection) is separate from per-breaker tuning.

Tomáš Novák: from the incident reduction angle: during a Sev1 we want as few people touching prod knobs as possible.

Tomáš Novák: esp bc flapping risk if someone tweaks cooldown w/out understanding signal delays.

Peter Holtz: what’s our actual current RBAC?

Peter Holtz: i thought only SRE oncall has access to `breakerctl` in prod, but i’ve seen platform folks run it in staging.

Christine Wong: prod is behind the “Reliability-Prod-Operators” okta group. platform folks can’t run prod commands unless they’re in that group.

Owen Phillips: but during the last overload incident, we had folks asking “can i just flip the breaker open for model X in us-east?”. we need the answer in the runbook.

Dev Patel: + also support needs a clear escalation path (who to page if customer asks “can you turn this off”).

Sean Gallagher: constraints for decision:
- we need a single accountable role during incident (IC / primary oncall)
- changes must be reversible + logged
- we can allow emergency disable (feature flag) if it’s causing harm, but only w/ IC approval

Sean Gallagher: otherwise we’ll end up with 5 people tweaking thresholds and making it impossible to reason about impact.

Rafael Mendes: proposal (tell me if anyone objects):
A) Only the acting Incident Commander (IC) *or* the eng-sre primary oncall can change breaker configs in prod.
B) Any change requires posting in #incidents thread with: scope, reason, expected effect, and rollback plan.
C) Non-SRE engineers can propose a change, but cannot execute unless temporarily added to the okta group by SRE manager / director.

Rafael Mendes: plus we make a short “allowed knobs” list so people don’t go off-script.

Christine Wong: on A: i’m okay with IC or SRE primary. but IC isn’t always SRE. sometimes product ICs. do they have the tooling access?

Rafael Mendes: good point. “IC” might not have prod access. we can phrase it as:
- executor: SRE primary oncall (or SRE secondary if primary is heads down)
- approver: IC

Tomáš Novák: +1 executor/approver split.

Peter Holtz: agree. also we should define “emergency actions” vs “tuning actions”.

Peter Holtz: emergency:
- disable overload protection flag for a region/model (if it’s broken)
- force breaker OPEN to stop cascades (rare)

Peter Holtz: tuning (should be avoided during active incident unless clearly needed):
- adjust thresholds/cooldown

Owen Phillips: do we ever want “force CLOSED” as emergency? sounds dangerous.

Christine Wong: pls no “force CLOSED” during overload. that’s basically “let everything in”. if you want that, disable the whole thing + accept blast radius.

Sean Gallagher: +1. no force closed.

Dev Patel: for support/runbook: can we have a one-liner:
“Support cannot request custom breaker changes; escalate to SRE oncall who will decide based on platform health.”

Rafael Mendes: yep.

Connor O'Brien: release/ops angle: if we’re changing configs we should also note whether it’s persisted or ephemeral.

Connor O'Brien: do changes go into config store (survive deploy) or just runtime override?

Christine Wong: today we have both:
- config store update (persists)
- temporary override via admin endpoint (expires after TTL)

Christine Wong: i’d strongly prefer incidents use TTL override only, unless we’ve decided it’s the new steady-state.

Tomáš Novák: +1. persistent changes during incident = future surprises.

Rafael Mendes: ok let’s codify:
- use TTL override for incident mitigations (default TTL 60m)
- post-incident follow-up ticket if change should be made permanent

Nora Ahmed: comms/status page: if we’re actively shedding, we sometimes message “we’re rate limiting”.

Nora Ahmed: can we add guidance for when it’s okay to say “load shedding is active” vs “degraded performance”? (bc those changes come with config flips)

Rafael Mendes: we can add a small note in runbook “if shed rate > X% for > Y min, coordinate with IC on status page update” and point to template.

Sean Gallagher: keep it lightweight in this thread. but yes, link to template.

Peter Holtz: tooling detail: can we add the exact command pattern in runbook so oncall doesn’t have to remember flags.

Christine Wong: sure. current syntax (subject to change but fine for runbook):
```
# Show current state/config
breakerctl get --region us-east --model rw-llama-70b --tier hosted

# Apply TTL override (recommended during incident)
breakerctl override --region us-east --model rw-llama-70b --tier hosted \
  --set cooldown_seconds=90 --set open_threshold=0.92 --ttl 60m \
  --reason "INC-#### reduce flapping during spike"

# Emergency disable via feature flag (requires IC approval)
flagctl set overload_protection.enabled \
  --region us-east --model rw-llama-70b --value false \
  --reason "INC-#### suspected bad breaker behavior"
```

Owen Phillips: what about permissions for `flagctl`? same okta group?

Christine Wong: yes, both are gated by Reliability-Prod-Operators.

Rafael Mendes: we should also add “two-person rule” for disabling the whole system?

Tomáš Novák: at least “IC approval + SRE executor” is basically that.

Sean Gallagher: agree. don’t add extra ceremony that slows mitigation, but require explicit IC ack in-thread.

Dev Patel: can we define who can add people to the okta group in an emergency? bc sometimes we need platform help.

Rafael Mendes: yes. add to runbook:
- default: nobody added ad-hoc
- exception: SRE Director (Sean) or SRE Manager (me) can add for up to 24h, must be documented in incident thread

Sean Gallagher: yep.

Peter Holtz: last point: audit trail. do we log overrides somewhere besides slack?

Christine Wong: breakerctl writes to audit log index `audit.prod.controlplane` with actor + diff + ttl. and incident-bot is going to snapshot breaker states per incident anyway.

incident-bot: :notebook: Reminder: For overload incidents, please capture:
• breaker states (open/half-open/closed) per impacted (region, model, tier)
• shed rate by reason
• queue depth / saturation signals
• any manual overrides applied

Rafael Mendes: ok, summarizing decision for runbook (reply if objections):
- Executor: eng-sre primary oncall (backup: eng-sre secondary)
- Approver: acting IC (must explicitly approve in incident thread)
- Allowed incident actions:
  1) TTL override of breaker parameters (preferred)
  2) force breaker OPEN (rare; only to stop cascade)
  3) disable overload protection via feature flag (only if suspected faulty; requires IC approval)
- Disallowed:
  - force breaker CLOSED
  - persistent config store changes during incident (unless explicitly agreed as new baseline; otherwise file follow-up)
- Access control:
  - prod tools gated by Okta group Reliability-Prod-Operators
  - temporary access grants only by Rafael (SRE Mgr) or Sean (SRE Dir), max 24h, documented in incident thread

Rafael Mendes: i’ll push this into the runbook + add the command snippets Christine posted.

Sean Gallagher: good. ship it.

Tomáš Novák: +1

Christine Wong: +1 i’ll sanity check the command examples before merge.

Owen Phillips: :thumbsup: thanks. this will save us time next incident.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: pls tag me when runbook is updated, i’ll include it in release checklist for canary expansions.

Dev Patel: and i’ll update support macros to align (no promises of “we can turn it off”, only “we can investigate + share retry guidance”).
